name: VisuallyHidden
purpose: Keep a short authored name or equivalent context available to assistive technology without adding a visible layout footprint.
useWhen: A nearby visual already communicates the same short meaning but a control, state, or relationship still needs an accessible text equivalent.

avoidWhen.condition: The text is an essential instruction, visible state, error, focusable control, or asynchronous announcement.
avoidWhen.useInstead: Visible Text or the application-owned feedback and live-region pattern

composition: Place a short equivalent phrase in VisuallyHidden.Root at the semantic owner that needs it; keep focusable descendants and live-region policy outside Root.

rules.statement: Keep hidden text short, specific, and equivalent to the nearby visual meaning; do not hide information that benefits everyone.
Do not place keyboard-focusable or interactive descendants inside VisuallyHidden.Root.
Do not use VisuallyHidden as a substitute for deliberate visible feedback or application-owned live-region behavior.
Do not override Atom's authoritative hiding properties or confuse visually hidden content with aria-hidden decorative content.
Load styles.css or core.css plus visually-hidden.css.

commonMistakes.mistake: Hiding essential instructions, placing a focusable control inside Root, or adding aria-hidden to content that should name a control or state.
commonMistakes.correction: Keep essential content visible, name the semantic owner with short hidden text only when the visual equivalent is already present, and use aria-hidden only for decoration.

validation: Inspect the accessibility tree and confirm the hidden phrase contributes exactly once to the intended name or description.
Confirm the root has no layout footprint, no focusable descendants, and unchanged behavior across zoom, direction, and appearance.
